parts.name: Multiple-choice cloze
parts.instr: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.example: 0 — A enjoyed  B gained  C owned  D held → A
parts.title: The return of board games
paras: In the last decade, board games have (0) enjoyed a remarkable comeback. Cafés where customers pay a small [[1]] to play any of hundreds of games are opening in cities around the world, and some new games [[2]] millions of pounds from fans before they have even been produced.

So why are people turning away from screens and back to cardboard? Part of the answer [[3]] in the social side of playing. Sitting around a table with friends, people talk, laugh and argue in a way that is difficult to [[4]] online.
Designers have also [[5]] a long way since the days of simple dice-and-counter games. Modern games often involve complex strategies, beautiful artwork and stories that [[6]] as you play.

Not everyone is convinced that the trend is here to [[7]], however. Critics point out that many games are expensive and take hours to learn. But for now, at least, a growing number of people seem happy to swap their phones [[8]] a pack of cards for an evening.

q.expl: fee — плата за услугу или вход. Fare — плата за проезд, wage и salary — зарплата.
raise money — собирать деньги (например, через краудфандинг). Rise не берёт дополнения, а grow и lift с деньгами в таком значении не используются.
Устойчивое выражение: the answer lies in… — ответ кроется в… Rest используется с on (rests on).
recreate — воссоздать атмосферу, ощущение. Restore и repair — чинить, восстанавливать вещь; recover — поправляться или вернуть потерянное.
Идиома come a long way — сильно продвинуться, развиться. Go a long way значит другое: «во многом помочь».
О сюжете говорят the story unfolds — история разворачивается. Unwrap — развернуть подарок, undo — отменить или расстегнуть, uncover — раскрыть тайну (и требует дополнения).
Идиома be here to stay — прийти надолго, закрепиться. В этой фразе другие глаголы не используются.
swap A for B — поменять одно на другое. Swap with используют с человеком: swap seats with someone.

parts.name: Open cloze
parts.instr: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: The world's oldest trees
paras: Some of the oldest living things on Earth (0) are trees. In the mountains of California, there are pines that have been growing [[9]] more than four thousand years. What makes this even more remarkable is that they live in conditions [[10]] most plants would find impossible: thin soil, strong winds and very little rain.

Scientists believe that the harsh environment may actually be one of the reasons [[11]] the trees live so long. Because they grow extremely slowly, their wood is very dense, [[12]] protects them from insects and disease.

To protect the trees, their exact location is kept secret. [[13]] the past, visitors damaged several of them by taking pieces of bark home [[14]] souvenirs. Today, anyone [[15]] wants to see them must stay on marked paths, and [[16]] is allowed to touch the trees.

q.expl: Present Perfect Continuous + период: have been growing for more than four thousand years.
Определительное придаточное к conditions: conditions that/which most plants would find impossible.
the reason why — причина, по которой. Подойдёт и that.
После запятой which относится ко всей предыдущей мысли («плотная древесина») — и это защищает деревья. That после запятой не ставится.
In the past — в прошлом.
take sth home as a souvenir — увезти что-то на память (в качестве сувенира).
Придаточное к anyone: anyone who wants to see them…
Нужно подлежащее с отрицанием: nobody is allowed to touch the trees. No one — два слова, а в пропуск идёт одно.

parts.name: Word formation
parts.instr: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of some of the lines to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Why volunteer?
paras: More and more young people are spending part of their gap year (0) volunteering abroad. Teaching children, building schools or protecting wildlife can be a hugely [[17]] experience. Many volunteers say that it gave them a new sense of [[18]] and helped them to become more [[19]].

However, some experts are critical of so-called 'voluntourism'. They argue that short visits by [[20]] volunteers can sometimes do more harm than good. Children in care, for example, may suffer when a [[21]] of different helpers come and go every few weeks.
Before signing up, it is therefore [[22]] to research the organisation carefully. A good project will offer proper [[23]] and will be able to explain [[24]] how it benefits the local community.

q.expl: Перед существительным experience нужно прилагательное: rewarding — приносящий удовлетворение.
a sense of independence — чувство самостоятельности; после of нужно существительное.
become more confident — стать увереннее; после become more нужно прилагательное.
По смыслу вред приносят неопытные волонтёры: inexperienced. Без отрицательной приставки смысл ломается.
a succession of — череда, вереница (одних за другими). Ловушка: success — «успех», здесь не подходит.
it is essential to — очень важно, необходимо.
offer proper training — дать нормальную подготовку; нужно существительное.
К глаголу explain нужно наречие: explain clearly.

parts.name: Key word transformation
parts.instr: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between two and five words, including the word given.

q.expl: would rather + инфинитив без to: I would rather stay. Ошибка: would rather to stay.

q.first: It was a mistake to tell her the truth.
q.expl: Сожаление о прошлом поступке: shouldn't have + V3 — не надо было говорить.

q.expl: После although идёт предложение, а после in spite of — существительное: in spite of the rain.

q.first: Someone stole my bike last night.
q.expl: Конструкция have sth done — с тобой что-то случилось по чужой воле: I had my bike stolen.

q.first: 'Have you finished your homework?' my mum asked me.
q.expl: Косвенный общий вопрос: whether + прямой порядок слов + сдвиг времени: Present Perfect → Past Perfect.

q.first: There's no milk left in the fridge.
q.expl: Фразовый глагол run out of — закончиться (о запасах): we have run out of milk.

parts.name: Multiple choice
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a teenage glider pilot. For questions 31–36, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
parts.title: Up in the air
parts.subtitle: Seventeen-year-old Jake Miller flew a glider on his own before he was old enough to drive a car. Amy Shaw went to meet him.
paras: The first thing that strikes you about Jake Miller is how calm he is. While I nervously watch the gliders being pulled into the sky by a small plane at the end of the field, he is eating a sandwich and chatting to the instructors as if he were waiting for a bus. 'People expect pilots to be brave,' he says, 'but really it's about being patient. Most of the day you're just waiting for the right weather.'

Jake's interest began at the age of twelve, when his grandfather, a retired airline pilot, took him to an air show. 'I'd always assumed flying was something you needed to be rich to do,' he says. 'Then I found out that the gliding club near us offers cheap lessons for teenagers if you help out around the airfield.' Since then, he has spent most of his weekends here, washing aircraft, moving equipment and, eventually, flying.

His first solo flight came two years later, and he admits he hadn't expected it to happen that day. 'My instructor just climbed out of the back seat and said, "Off you go." I think if I'd known in advance, I wouldn't have slept the night before.' The flight lasted only eight minutes, but he remembers every second of it. 'It was the quietest place I've ever been. No engine, just the sound of the wind.'

Not everything has gone smoothly. Last summer, a sudden change in the weather forced him to land in a farmer's field several miles from the club. 'That was a long afternoon,' he laughs. 'The farmer wasn't exactly delighted to see me, and it took four hours to take the glider apart and drive it home on a trailer.' Rather than putting him off, though, the experience made him more determined to improve his understanding of weather.

His friends at school are less impressed than you might think. 'Most of them think it's a bit strange,' he says with a shrug. 'They'd rather spend Saturday playing football or gaming. That's fine – I used to be the same.' What he does find frustrating is that so few young people know gliding exists. Next month he is giving a talk at his school, and the club has agreed to offer a free trial flight to any student who comes along.

q.stem: What does Jake say about being a pilot?
opts: It requires more courage than people realise.
It involves spending a lot of time waiting.
It is less enjoyable than he had expected.
It is mainly about following instructions.
q.hl: Most of the day you're just waiting for the right weather.
q.expl: Джейк говорит, что главное — терпение, и большую часть дня просто ждёшь подходящей погоды. Ловушка A: он, наоборот, говорит, что смелость — это стереотип.

q.stem: What surprised Jake when he first became interested in flying?
opts: that his grandfather had been a pilot
that he could afford to learn
how much work was involved at the club
q.hl: Then I found out that the gliding club near us offers cheap lessons for teenagers
q.expl: Он думал, что летать могут только богатые, а потом узнал о дешёвых уроках для подростков, то есть учиться ему по карману. Работа на аэродроме — условие скидки, а не то, что его удивило.

q.stem: What does Jake suggest about his first solo flight?
opts: He felt he had not been properly prepared for it.
He was glad he had not known about it beforehand.
It was shorter than he had hoped.
q.hl: I think if I'd known in advance, I wouldn't have slept the night before.
q.expl: Если бы знал заранее, не спал бы ночь, значит, хорошо, что не знал. Тишину он описывает как приятное воспоминание, а не страх (D).

q.stem: How did Jake react to landing in the farmer's field?
opts: He decided to take fewer risks in future.
He was embarrassed by the farmer's reaction.
It made him want to learn more about the weather.
He realised how dangerous gliding could be.
q.hl: the experience made him more determined to improve his understanding of weather
q.expl: Случай не отпугнул его, а наоборот: он захотел лучше разбираться в погоде. Фермер был недоволен, но о том, что Джейку было стыдно, не сказано (B).

opts: His friends don't take his hobby seriously.
Few young people are aware that gliding exists.
The club doesn't do enough to attract new members.
He has less free time than his friends.
q.hl: What he does find frustrating is that so few young people know gliding exists.
q.expl: Прямо в тексте: его расстраивает, что мало кто знает о планеризме. Отношение друзей его не задевает: «That's fine» (A). Клуб, наоборот, предлагает бесплатные полёты (C).

q.stem: What is the writer's main purpose in the article?
opts: to persuade readers to try gliding
to warn about the dangers of flying at a young age
to give a portrait of a young person's passion for gliding
to compare gliding with other hobbies
q.hl: The first thing that strikes you about Jake Miller is how calm he is.
q.expl: Весь текст — портрет Джейка: его характер, путь, трудности и увлечённость. Автор не уговаривает читателя (A) и не пугает опасностями (B).

parts.name: Gapped text
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a woman who turned a car park into a garden. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
parts.title: From car park to garden
parts.subtitle: When the car park behind her block of flats was closed, Nadia Haddad decided to turn it into a garden. Here she describes how it happened.
paras: For years, the car park behind our building was the ugliest place in the neighbourhood. When the council finally closed it because the ground had become unsafe, most people assumed it would simply be fenced off and forgotten. [[37]] I had no experience of gardening at all, but I couldn't stop thinking about what the space could become.

My first step was to knock on every door in the building. I expected people to be suspicious, or simply not interested. [[38]] Within a week, more than thirty neighbours had signed up, including several elderly residents who had grown vegetables all their lives.

Getting permission from the council took much longer. There were forms to fill in, meetings to attend and endless questions about safety. [[39]] Eventually, after almost six months, we were given a two-year licence to use the land, on condition that we cleared it ourselves.

Clearing it was hard work. The surface was covered in broken concrete, and underneath there was almost no proper soil. [[40]] Local shops donated wood for raised beds, and a builder who lived nearby lent us a small digger for a weekend.

The first summer was a huge success. We grew tomatoes, beans and enough courgettes to feed the whole street. [[41]] Neighbours who had lived next to each other for decades without speaking now stop to chat every time they pass.

Our licence runs out next year, and nobody knows what will happen to the land after that. [[42]] Whatever happens, the people in our building are no longer strangers, and no one can take that away from us.

sents.A: I, on the other hand, saw an opportunity.
sents.B: In fact, the reaction was the complete opposite.
sents.C: At times, I was tempted to give up altogether.
sents.D: Luckily, we didn't have to do everything on our own.
sents.E: But the vegetables, in the end, were not the most important thing.
sents.F: The council has hinted that it may be sold to developers.
sents.G: Some of the older residents even started giving gardening classes.

q.expl: «Most people assumed it would be forgotten» — и контраст: «I, on the other hand, saw an opportunity» (A). Дальше она говорит, что не могла перестать думать о том, чем может стать это место.
Она ждала подозрительности и безразличия, а «the reaction was the complete opposite» (B): за неделю записались больше тридцати соседей.
Бесконечные формы и встречи → «I was tempted to give up» (C) → «Eventually… we were given a licence». Слово eventually показывает, что до этого было тяжело.
«We didn't have to do everything on our own» (D), а дальше примеры помощи: магазины подарили доски, строитель одолжил экскаватор.

Урожай был отличный, «but the vegetables… were not the most important thing» (E). Главное — соседи начали общаться. Ловушка G: про пожилых жильцов логично, но она не объясняет, почему дальше речь о разговорах соседей.
Никто не знает, что будет с землёй, → совет намекает, что её могут продать застройщикам (F). «Whatever happens» дальше отвечает на эту угрозу.

parts.name: Multiple matching
parts.instr: You are going to read an article in which four young people describe a book that changed their life. For questions 43–52, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.
parts.title: The book that changed my life

texts.name: Tom
texts.body: I was thirteen and stuck in a hospital bed with a broken leg when my aunt gave me a novel about a boy who sails around the world alone. To be honest, I only started it because there was nothing else to do – I'd never been much of a reader. But by the second chapter I was hooked. What stayed with me wasn't the adventure itself so much as the boy's attitude: he never waited for someone else to solve his problems. Since then, I've been saving every penny from my part-time job, and next summer I'm going to cycle across Europe with a friend. My aunt says she takes full responsibility.

texts.name: Aisha
texts.body: The book that changed things for me was a popular science book about how the brain works. English isn't my first language, so the first few chapters were really hard going – I had a dictionary open next to me the whole time. My dad, who's a doctor, ended up reading it too, and we'd discuss a chapter every evening over dinner. That's probably my favourite memory of it, actually. Until then I'd been planning to study law, but the book made me realise that what really fascinates me is why people behave the way they do. I start a psychology degree in September.

texts.name: Leo
texts.body: My swimming coach lent me the autobiography of an Olympic athlete just after I'd quit the team. I'd lost three races in a row and decided I wasn't good enough. I almost didn't read it – I thought it would be full of the usual stuff about believing in yourself. Instead, it was surprisingly honest about how often she had failed, and how close she had come to giving up herself. It made me see that losing is just part of the process. I went back to training the following month, and although I'm still not winning much, I enjoy it far more than I used to.

texts.name: Mei
texts.body: My parents always thought comics were a waste of time, so I read my first graphic novel secretly, under the covers at night. It told the story of a family escaping a war, and I couldn't believe a comic could be so moving. I've read it at least ten times since then, and I notice something new in the drawings every time. It inspired me to start drawing my own stories, and last year one of them won a regional competition. Even my parents came to the prize-giving – I think they've finally changed their minds.

q.stem: wasn't keen on reading before discovering the book?
q.hl: I'd never been much of a reader
q.expl: Том начал книгу только от скуки в больнице: «I'd never been much of a reader».

q.stem: shared the experience of reading the book with a family member?
q.hl: we'd discuss a chapter every evening over dinner
q.expl: Айша с папой обсуждали по главе каждый вечер. Ловушка A: тётя подарила книгу, но не читала её вместе с Томом.

q.hl: My swimming coach lent me the autobiography
q.expl: Лео дал книгу тренер по плаванию сразу после того, как Лео ушёл из команды.

q.stem: had to hide the fact that they were reading the book?
q.hl: I read my first graphic novel secretly
q.expl: Мэй читала тайком, под одеялом, потому что родители считали комиксы пустой тратой времени.

q.stem: changed their plans for their education as a result of the book?
q.hl: Until then I'd been planning to study law

q.hl: I thought it would be full of the usual stuff about believing in yourself

q.expl: Тома зацепило не приключение, а отношение героя: он никогда не ждал, что его проблемы решит кто-то другой.

q.hl: although I'm still not winning much, I enjoy it far more than I used to
